ambiguities.text: The specification doesn't define behavior when Snappy decompression fails (corrupted data).
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume decompression failure results in message rejection and potentially peer disconnection, similar to other protocol violations.

ambiguities.text: The statement 'Snappy framing is not used' could be misinterpreted given multiple Snappy variants.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume raw Snappy block compression is used (not streaming framing format), as DEVp2p is already message-oriented.

ambiguities.text: The 16MB limit is mentioned but whether this applies per-message or per-batch is unclear.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume 16MB is the per-message limit matching existing DEVp2p message size constraints.

implicit_assumptions.description: The Snappy library implementation is free of vulnerabilities (buffer overflows, etc.).
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Malformed compressed data could exploit library bugs to achieve remote code execution.

implicit_assumptions.description: Nodes have sufficient memory to buffer 16MB decompressed messages.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Memory exhaustion attacks possible if nodes accept many concurrent large messages.

implicit_assumptions.description: An attacker cannot construct valid Snappy streams that bypass the size check but expand beyond limits.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Decompression bombs could cause denial of service via memory exhaustion.

implicit_assumptions.description: Version negotiation happens before any compressed messages are sent.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Attempting to decompress uncompressed v4 messages would cause parsing failures.
